Within-set affinities (0.345–0.703) exceed all between-set affinities (0.080–0.178), and the nearest competing boundaries are K7_C0001–K7_C0004, K7_C0002–K7_C0003, and K7_C0001–K7_C0007. This is partition-level patient-geometry concordance only; it does not establish biological meaning or clinical validity, and it does not by itself determine any accept, drop, split, or merge action.

reports.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural screen evaluates internal graph structure and nearest-pair boundaries of the current candidate partition on the candidate-generation consensus geometry. All seven sets show their dominant spectral gap at the single-cluster resolution (screen_candidate_k=1), so the screen does not identify a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal in any set; the large leading eigengaps (0.699–1.167) are consistent with dominance of the single-cluster resolution and should not be read as evidence of internal substructure. Within-set affinities (0.345–0.703) exceed all between-set affinities (0.080–0.178), and the nearest competing boundaries are K7_C0001–K7_C0004, K7_C0002–K7_C0003, and K7_C0001–K7_C0007. Overall the native-view structural pattern is coherent at the partition level, but it is triage evidence only: it does not establish biological meaning, clinical validity, or any accept, drop, split, or merge action.
reports.cross_evidence_context: No prior reports or additional modality-specific evidence are present in this round; the assessment rests solely on the partition structural diagnostics. The nearest-pair affinities identify boundaries for possible pair review but do not themselves prescribe merging, and the absence of a subdivision signal is neither positive nor negative evidence about independence from neighboring candidates.

Bootstrap intervals are narrow and non-degenerate (1000 valid replicates), so the significant pairs are not driven by a few patients. This is partition-level patient-geometry concordance only; it does not establish biological meaning or clinical validity, and it does not by itself determine any accept, drop, split, or merge action.

reports.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural screen evaluates internal graph structure and nearest-pair boundaries of the current candidate partition on the candidate-generation consensus geometry. All seven sets show their dominant spectral gap at the single-cluster resolution (screen_candidate_k=1), so the screen does not identify a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal in any set; the large leading eigengaps (0.699–1.167) are consistent with dominance of the single-cluster resolution and should not be read as evidence of internal substructure. Within-set affinities (0.345–0.703) exceed all between-set affinities (0.080–0.178), and the nearest competing boundaries are K7_C0001–K7_C0004, K7_C0002–K7_C0003, and K7_C0001–K7_C0007. reports.cross_evidence_context: No prior reports or additional modality-specific evidence are present in this round; the assessment rests solely on the partition structural diagnostics. reports.dimension_interpretation: K7_C0002 shows a coherent and interpretable molecular phenotype relative to the rest of the partition, dominated by strong, globally adjusted-significant depletion of VHL mutation (0/16 vs 56/87; OR 0.017, q_global 0.0024) together with directionally consistent PBRM1 depletion (OR 0.193, q_driver 0.129). TP53 enrichment is driver-panel-adjusted significant (OR 45.4, q_driver 0.024) but not globally adjusted-significant (q_global 1.0), and KDM5C enrichment is nominal only (q_driver 0.175). CDKN2A is not estimable because neither group has events. The VHL-depleted pattern is the most robust single signal and is consistent with the previously reported immune-low/metabolism-high transcriptomic phenotype for this set, but biological identity does not by itself establish that current membership or granularity deserves independent retention.
reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior RNA pathway enrichment for K7_C0002 reported strong down-regulation of immune/inflammatory programs and up-regulation of oxidative phosphorylation, and prior native-geometry membership alignment for K7_C0002 was coherently negative across all four modalities. The WXS VHL-depletion signal adds a molecular axis consistent with the immune-low phenotype but does not resolve the negative geometric membership representation.
limitations: Set-versus-rest contrast: the rest combines six other candidate sets and may be heterogeneous.
Small target set (n=16) and zero-event cells produce very wide odds-ratio intervals and require Haldane-Anscombe correction.

reports.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, multiple measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show BH-adjusted-significant association with the partition geometry: tissue source site (r_squared 0.204, PERMDISP not significant), CT phase (0.154, PERMDISP significant), slice thickness (0.136), z-spacing (0.142), CT manufacturer (0.059, PERMDISP significant), pixel spacing (0.019), and study year (0.029). Reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and scanner model (q=0.054) are suggestive but not adjusted-significant, and their PERMDISP tests are not estimable because some levels have fewer than two observations. This indicates a partition-wide technical concern that may motivate candidate-specific follow-up, but partition-scope association must not be presented as a candidate-specific confounder association. Association is not causation, and a significant PERMANOVA is not proof of technical artifact; conversely, nonsignificance would not establish absence of confounding. PERMANOVA, PERMDISP, and continuous distance-regression p-values belong to separate BH families and are not pooled.
reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior candidate-specific confounder reports found adjusted-significant associations for K7_C0003 (site, manufacturer, scanner model, kernel, slice thickness, z-spacing), K7_C0004 (phase, manufacturer, slice thickness, z-spacing), and K7_C0005 (site, z-spacing), while K7_C0001, K7_C0002, K7_C0006, and K7_C0007 showed no adjusted-significant candidate-specific associations. The partition-scope results here describe a partition-wide technical concern and do not by themselves localize confounding to any candidate.
limitations: Partition-scope association describes a partition-wide technical concern and must not be presented as a candidate-specific confounder association.
Association is not causation; a significant PERMANOVA is not proof of technical artifact.
PERMDISP is not estimable for reconstruction kernel and scanner model because some levels have fewer than two observations.

Bootstrap intervals are narrow and non-degenerate (1000 valid replicates), so the significant pairs are not driven by a few patients. This is partition-level patient-geometry concordance only; it does not establish biological meaning or clinical validity, and it does not by itself determine any accept, drop, split, or merge action.

cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural screen evaluates internal graph structure and nearest-pair boundaries of the current candidate partition on the candidate-generation consensus geometry. All seven sets show their dominant spectral gap at the single-cluster resolution (screen_candidate_k=1), so the screen does not identify a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal in any set; the large leading eigengaps (0.699–1.167) are consistent with dominance of the single-cluster resolution and should not be read as evidence of internal substructure. Within-set affinities (0.345–0.703) exceed all between-set affinities (0.080–0.178), and the nearest competing boundaries are K7_C0001–K7_C0004, K7_C0002–K7_C0003, and K7_C0001–K7_C0007. Overall the native-view structural pattern is coherent at the partition level, but it is triage evidence only: it does not establish biological meaning, clinical validity, or any accept, drop, split, or merge action.

The nearest-pair affinities identify boundaries for possible pair review but do not themselves prescribe merging, and the absence of a subdivision signal is neither positive nor negative evidence about independence from neighboring candidates.

CT (0.087) and WSI (0.110) show small positive silhouettes with within-distance below between-distance and low negative fractions (0.15), while RNA (-0.072) and WXS (-0.233) show negative silhouettes with within-distance exceeding between-distance and high negative fractions (0.85, 0.80). Synthesized jointly rather than by vote counting, the pattern is conflicting: two modalities weakly represent the membership and two do not. In RNA and WXS the nearest competing set (K7_C0004 and K7_C0001 respectively) is closer than the member's own set. This bears directly on membership representation but does not by itself determine accept or drop and does not establish biological or clinical meaning.

The conflicting set-level membership geometry here is a different scope (membership vs pair boundary) and does not contradict those pair-level observations.

reports.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural screen evaluates internal graph structure and nearest-pair boundaries of the current candidate partition on the candidate-generation consensus geometry. All seven sets show their dominant spectral gap at the single-cluster resolution (screen_candidate_k=1), so the screen does not identify a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal in any set; the large leading eigengaps (0.699–1.167) are consistent with dominance of the single-cluster resolution and should not be read as evidence of internal substructure. Within-set affinities (0.345–0.703) exceed all between-set affinities (0.080–0.178), and the nearest competing boundaries are K7_C0001–K7_C0004, K7_C0002–K7_C0003, and K7_C0001–K7_C0007. Overall the native-view structural pattern is coherent at the partition level, but it is triage evidence only: it does not establish biological meaning, clinical validity, or any accept, drop, split, or merge action.
reports.cross_evidence_context: No prior reports or additional modality-specific evidence are present in this round; the assessment rests solely on the partition structural diagnostics. The nearest-pair affinities identify boundaries for possible pair review but do not themselves prescribe merging, and the absence of a subdivision signal is neither positive nor negative evidence about independence from neighboring candidates.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For K7_C0004, the four native patient geometries provide weak and conflicting evidence about membership representation. RNA shows a small positive separation (silhouette 0.044; within 0.870 vs between 0.908; negative fraction 0.28), while CT (-0.017) and WSI (-0.004) are essentially at zero and WXS is clearly negative (-0.317; within 0.814 vs between 0.576; negative fraction 0.78). Synthesizing jointly rather than by vote counting, the pattern is weak/conflicting: one modality weakly represents the membership, two are negligible, and one does not. In CT and WXS the nearest competing set (K7_C0005 and K7_C0001 respectively) is closer than the member's own set, indicating the current membership is not the nearest geometric grouping in those views. This bears directly on membership representation but does not by itself determine accept or drop and does not establish biological or clinical meaning.
reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior partition-level structural diagnostics reported within-set affinities exceeding between-set affinities with nearest competing boundaries including K7_C0001-K7_C0004, and a single-cluster-dominated spectral screen; the set-level native-view results here show that this partition-level coherence is not reflected in individual native geometries for K7_C0004. Prior pair-level reports for K7_C0001-K7_C0004 and K7_C0002-K7_C0004 described weak or mixed boundary representation, consistent with the weak set-level pattern seen here. Prior biological reports describe K7_C0004 as an immune-low/proliferation-low phenotype, which is identity evidence and does not bear on geometric membership representation.

reports.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, multiple measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show BH-adjusted-significant association with the partition geometry: tissue source site (r_squared 0.204, PERMDISP not significant), CT phase (0.154, PERMDISP significant), slice thickness (0.136), z-spacing (0.142), CT manufacturer (0.059, PERMDISP significant), pixel spacing (0.019), and study year (0.029). Reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and scanner model (q=0.054) are suggestive but not adjusted-significant, and their PERMDISP tests are not estimable because some levels have fewer than two observations. This indicates a partition-wide technical concern that may motivate candidate-specific follow-up, but partition-scope association must not be presented as a candidate-specific confounder association. Association is not causation, and a significant PERMANOVA is not proof of technical artifact; conversely, nonsignificance would not establish absence of confounding. PERMANOVA, PERMDISP, and continuous distance-regression p-values belong to separate BH families and are not pooled.
reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior candidate-specific confounder reports found adjusted-significant associations for K7_C0003 (site, manufacturer, scanner model, kernel, slice thickness, z-spacing), K7_C0004 (phase, manufacturer, slice thickness, z-spacing), and K7_C0005 (site, z-spacing), while K7_C0001, K7_C0002, K7_C0006, and K7_C0007 showed no adjusted-significant candidate-specific associations. The partition-scope results here describe a partition-wide technical concern and do not by themselves localize confounding to any candidate.
limitations: Partition-scope association describes a partition-wide technical concern and must not be presented as a candidate-specific confounder association.

cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, the four native patient geometries show modest but statistically significant overall concordance for three of six modality pairs: WSI-RNA (GRV 0.198, p=0.001), CT-WSI (0.167, p=0.001), and RNA-WXS (0.145, p=0.001). The remaining three pairs are weak and not permutation-significant: CT-WXS (0.103, p=0.218), CT-RNA (0.092, p=0.071), and WSI-WXS (0.092, p=0.096). Bootstrap intervals are narrow and non-degenerate (1000 valid replicates), so the significant pairs are not driven by a few patients. This is partition-level patient-geometry concordance only; it does not establish biological meaning or clinical validity, and it does not by itself determine any accept, drop, split, or merge action.
cross_modal_consistency.cross_evidence_context: Prior set- and pair-level native-geometry reports showed substantial cross-modal disagreement in membership and boundary representation (e.g., WXS often separating while CT, RNA, and WSI did not). The partition-level GRV results here show that overall patient-geometry structure is only modestly shared across modalities, with CT least concordant with the molecular views, which is consistent with the earlier pattern of material cross-modal disagreement.
limitations: GRV is overall shared structure between native distance matrices, not mechanistic agreement or independent validation.

reports.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural screen evaluates internal graph structure and nearest-pair boundaries of the current candidate partition on the candidate-generation consensus geometry. All seven sets show their dominant spectral gap at the single-cluster resolution (screen_candidate_k=1), so the screen does not identify a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal in any set; the large leading eigengaps (0.699–1.167) are consistent with dominance of the single-cluster resolution and should not be read as evidence of internal substructure. Within-set affinities (0.345–0.703) exceed all between-set affinities (0.080–0.178), and the nearest competing boundaries are K7_C0001–K7_C0004, K7_C0002–K7_C0003, and K7_C0001–K7_C0007. Overall the native-view structural pattern is coherent at the partition level, but it is triage evidence only: it does not establish biological meaning, clinical validity, or any accept, drop, split, or merge action.
reports.cross_evidence_context: No prior reports or additional modality-specific evidence are present in this round; the assessment rests solely on the partition structural diagnostics. The nearest-pair affinities identify boundaries for possible pair review but do not themselves prescribe merging, and the absence of a subdivision signal is neither positive nor negative evidence about independence from neighboring candidates.

The nearest-pair affinities identify boundaries for possible pair review but do not themselves prescribe merging, and the absence of a subdivision signal is neither positive nor negative evidence about independence from neighboring candidates.

reports.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural screen evaluates internal graph structure and nearest-pair boundaries of the current candidate partition on the candidate-generation consensus geometry. All seven sets show their dominant spectral gap at the single-cluster resolution (screen_candidate_k=1), so the screen does not identify a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal in any set; the large leading eigengaps (0.699–1.167) are consistent with dominance of the single-cluster resolution and should not be read as evidence of internal substructure. Within-set affinities (0.345–0.703) exceed all between-set affinities (0.080–0.178), and the nearest competing boundaries are K7_C0001–K7_C0004, K7_C0002–K7_C0003, and K7_C0001–K7_C0007. Overall the native-view structural pattern is coherent at the partition level, but it is triage evidence only: it does not establish biological meaning, clinical validity, or any accept, drop, split, or merge action.
reports.cross_evidence_context: No prior reports or additional modality-specific evidence are present in this round; the assessment rests solely on the partition structural diagnostics. The nearest-pair affinities identify boundaries for possible pair review but do not themselves prescribe merging, and the absence of a subdivision signal is neither positive nor negative evidence about independence from neighboring candidates.
limitations: Structural diagnostics are computed on the candidate-generation consensus geometry, which is not external validation or a stability score.

Bootstrap intervals are narrow and non-degenerate (1000 valid replicates), so the significant pairs are not driven by a few patients. This is partition-level patient-geometry concordance only; it does not establish biological meaning or clinical validity, and it does not by itself determine any accept, drop, split, or merge action.
reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior set- and pair-level native-geometry reports showed substantial cross-modal disagreement in membership and boundary representation (e.g., WXS often separating while CT, RNA, and WSI did not). The partition-level GRV results here show that overall patient-geometry structure is only modestly shared across modalities, with CT least concordant with the molecular views, which is consistent with the earlier pattern of material cross-modal disagreement.

cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, the four native patient geometries show modest but statistically significant overall concordance for three of six modality pairs: WSI-RNA (GRV 0.198, p=0.001), CT-WSI (0.167, p=0.001), and RNA-WXS (0.145, p=0.001). The remaining three pairs are weak and not permutation-significant: CT-WXS (0.103, p=0.218), CT-RNA (0.092, p=0.071), and WSI-WXS (0.092, p=0.096). Bootstrap intervals are narrow and non-degenerate (1000 valid replicates), so the significant pairs are not driven by a few patients. This is partition-level patient-geometry concordance only; it does not establish biological meaning or clinical validity, and it does not by itself determine any accept, drop, split, or merge action.
cross_modal_consistency.cross_evidence_context: Prior set- and pair-level native-geometry reports showed substantial cross-modal disagreement in membership and boundary representation (e.g., WXS often separating while CT, RNA, and WSI did not). The partition-level GRV results here show that overall patient-geometry structure is only modestly shared across modalities, with CT least concordant with the molecular views, which is consistent with the earlier pattern of material cross-modal disagreement.

reports.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural screen evaluates internal graph structure and nearest-pair boundaries of the current candidate partition on the candidate-generation consensus geometry. All seven sets show their dominant spectral gap at the single-cluster resolution (screen_candidate_k=1), so the screen does not identify a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal in any set; the large leading eigengaps (0.699–1.167) are consistent with dominance of the single-cluster resolution and should not be read as evidence of internal substructure. Within-set affinities (0.345–0.703) exceed all between-set affinities (0.080–0.178), and the nearest competing boundaries are K7_C0001–K7_C0004, K7_C0002–K7_C0003, and K7_C0001–K7_C0007. Overall the native-view structural pattern is coherent at the partition level, but it is triage evidence only: it does not establish biological meaning, clinical validity, or any accept, drop, split, or merge action.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For K7_C0007, the four native patient geometries provide conflicting evidence about membership representation. WXS shows maximal separation (silhouette 1.0; within 0.0 vs between 0.536; negative fraction 0.0), while CT (-0.086), RNA (-0.153), and WSI (-0.329) all show negative mean silhouettes with within-distance exceeding between-distance and high negative fractions (0.5, 1.0, 1.0). Synthesizing jointly rather than by vote counting, the pattern is conflicting: one modality fully represents the current membership and three do not. In CT, RNA, and WSI the nearest competing set (K7_C0003, K7_C0001, K7_C0001 respectively) is closer than the member's own set, indicating the current membership is not the nearest geometric grouping in those views. This bears directly on membership representation but does not by itself determine accept or drop and does not establish biological or clinical meaning.
reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior partition-level structural diagnostics reported within-set affinities exceeding between-set affinities with nearest competing boundaries including K7_C0001-K7_C0007, and a single-cluster-dominated spectral screen; the set-level native-view results here show that this partition-level coherence is not reflected in individual native geometries for K7_C0007. Prior pair-level reports for K7_C0001-K7_C0007, K7_C0003-K7_C0007, and K7_C0004-K7_C0007 described conflicting or weak boundary representation, consistent with the conflicting set-level pattern seen here. Prior biological reports describe K7_C0007 as a proliferation-high/immune-low phenotype, which is identity evidence and does not bear on geometric membership representation.

reports.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, the four native patient geometries show modest but statistically significant overall concordance for three of six modality pairs: WSI-RNA (GRV 0.198, p=0.001), CT-WSI (0.167, p=0.001), and RNA-WXS (0.145, p=0.001). The remaining three pairs are weak and not permutation-significant: CT-WXS (0.103, p=0.218), CT-RNA (0.092, p=0.071), and WSI-WXS (0.092, p=0.096). Bootstrap intervals are narrow and non-degenerate (1000 valid replicates), so the significant pairs are not driven by a few patients. This is partition-level patient-geometry concordance only; it does not establish biological meaning or clinical validity, and it does not by itself determine any accept, drop, split, or merge action.
reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior set- and pair-level native-geometry reports showed substantial cross-modal disagreement in membership and boundary representation (e.g., WXS often separating while CT, RNA, and WSI did not). The partition-level GRV results here show that overall patient-geometry structure is only modestly shared across modalities, with CT least concordant with the molecular views, which is consistent with the earlier pattern of material cross-modal disagreement.
limitations: GRV is overall shared structure between native distance matrices, not mechanistic agreement or independent validation.
Partition-level concordance does not localize to any candidate set or pair and must not be promoted to a candidate-specific claim.
Three of six modality pairs are not permutation-significant; nonsignificance does not establish absence of shared structure.
Permutation p-values are one-sided under exchangeable patient correspondence and are not action thresholds.
